description:
Reduce the per-call cost of the bit-backend threshold read so the pinned non-regression comparison passes without changing the predeclared tolerance.

## Background

The post-cutover receipt of `50b47eae`, `dev/benchmarks/tuning_profiles/2026-08-20-post-cutover-receipt.md`, records `RESULT: FAIL` against the baseline at two of the thirty-four pinned cells: `bit_backend/popcount/words=1` rises from 1.853240 to 2.191107 ns/call, a ratio of 1.182311, and `bit_backend/popcount/words=8` rises from 3.501248 to 3.726078 ns/call, a ratio of 1.064214. Both exceed the predeclared `tau_cell` of 5 %. The whole-set `tau_set` holds at 0.998853.

The across-build control arm predeclared by `51058f8e` sits at 0.972476 and 1.002702 at those two cells, so the reading fixed in `across-build-control-arm-v1.md` section 4.3 before any of these numbers existed attributes the excursion to the cutover rather than to the across-build component. The excursion is not noise: every execution of the post-cutover arm stands above every execution of the baseline at `words=1`, and no cell's own dispersion reaches `tau_cell`.

The mechanism is the one `dev/active/220cab0b/design.md` section 8 describes — `select_backend_for_size` performs a `OnceLock` resolution per call at the selection boundary, and at the cheapest bit-logical operations that cost is a material fraction of the whole operation. What the measurement contradicts is that design's assessment of the cost as thin, not its account of where the cost is paid.

Owner decision DEC-D (2026-08-20) resolves this by removing the cost rather than by widening the tolerance or amending the epic's criterion.

**A compiled-in floor below which the profile is not consulted does not solve it.** Such a floor removes the read only below itself, so fixing `words=8` would require a floor above 8. The conservative default is 8 and the committed host calibration of `5ecc9bf8` selects 4 for this field, so any floor high enough to fix `words=8` would put the boundary beyond the profile's reach and make the calibration inert. The cost must therefore be reduced while the profile keeps governing the boundary at every pinned size.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The per-call cost of resolving `bit_backend.simd_min_words` at the selection boundary is reduced, and the profile still governs the boundary at every size in the pinned set, including a calibrated value of 4 below the conservative default of 8.
- [hard] REQ-02: `select_backend_for_size` keeps its current selection semantics exactly: the same comparison operator and sense, the same conservative default when no profile is installed, and the same behaviour in a build without the `simd` feature.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test observes that an installed profile whose `simd_min_words` differs from the default still moves the selected route, including a value below the conservative default, so the reduction does not come at the cost of tunability.
- [hard] REQ-04: `dev/active/220cab0b/design.md` section 4.1 records the mechanism and the measurement that motivates it, added without rewriting the document's existing citations, which are anchored at commit `05bc9c14`.
- [hard] REQ-05: The change is confined to the resolution mechanism. No in-source default value moves, no pinned cell changes, the `selector-non-regression-v1` schema token is not bumped, and `crates/gf2-core/src/field/poly.rs` is untouched.

## Notes

Whether the reduction is sufficient is decided by a fresh run of the pinned procedure under `50b47eae`, not by this issue. This issue delivers the mechanism; `50b47eae` re-measures it.
title: Reduce the per-call cost of the bit-backend threshold read
